LegalTerms.title: Terms and conditions
LegalTerms.lede: Immonation GmbH · Nürnberger Straße 18 · 90513 Zirndorf · As of July 2026. The German version is authoritative.

sections.heading: § 1 Scope and contracting parties
paragraphs: (1) These terms and conditions apply to all contracts and services between Immonation GmbH (hereinafter “Immonation”) and its customers — via the website https://www.immonationgmbh.de as well as under any agreement concluded between the parties.

(2) A customer within the meaning of these terms is the seller or buyer of a property and, in exceptional cases, also the landlord or — subject to the “Bestellerprinzip” — the person seeking a tenancy. The principal contract is the purchase, rental, or lease contract brokered in each case.

(3) A consumer is any natural person who concludes the contract predominantly for private purposes (Section 13 BGB); an entrepreneur is anyone acting in the exercise of a commercial or independent professional activity (Section 14 BGB).
(4) Individually agreed terms and property-specific commission disclosures take precedence over these terms (Section 305b BGB).

sections.heading: § 2 Subject matter and formation of the contract
paragraphs: (1) Immonation provides brokerage services in the form of evidencing the opportunity to conclude a contract or brokering such a contract concerning real estate.

(2) The contract is formed when the customer makes use of Immonation’s services — in particular by retrieving an exposé or further property information, arranging a viewing, or entering into negotiations — after Immonation has appeared recognizably as broker and has quantified its commission claim for the success case.
(3) Evidencing or brokering a purchase contract for an apartment or single-family house to a consumer requires text form (Section 656a BGB).
(4) Where the parties have a separate written agreement, its provisions take precedence over these terms in the event of conflict.

sections.heading: § 3 Services, offers, and property information
paragraphs: (1) The scope of services follows the agreement in each case and includes in particular valuation, preparation of documents, marketing, qualification of prospects, viewings, and support through to the notary appointment.
(2) Immonation’s offers are non-binding and subject to change. Prior sale, price changes, and error are reserved.

(3) Property-related information regularly originates from the owner, seller, property manager, authorities, or other third parties. Immonation forwards this carefully but assumes no warranty for accuracy, completeness, or currency unless it knew or ought to have known of the inaccuracy. Checking information material to the customer’s decision is the customer’s responsibility.

sections.heading: § 4 Customer cooperation and power of attorney
paragraphs: (1) The customer provides the documents and information required for marketing completely and accurately.

(2) Under the separate agreement, the seller authorizes Immonation in particular to inspect the land register and official files and to request and receive required documents from authorities and the notary. Where separately agreed, this power of attorney continues for up to twelve months after conclusion of the principal contract for the purpose of reviewing the causality of the brokerage activity.

sections.heading: § 5 Commission claim and amount
paragraphs: (1) The commission claim arises as soon as a valid principal contract is concluded as a result of Immonation’s evidencing or brokerage (Section 652 BGB). It is sufficient that Immonation’s activity was a contributing cause of the contract conclusion.
(2) On a sale, the commission is 3.57% including 19% VAT of the notarized purchase price per contracting party (seller and buyer side), unless otherwise agreed for the specific property.

(3) If Immonation acts for both sides when a consumer purchases an apartment or single-family house, it may only have commission promised by both parties in equal amounts (Section 656c BGB). If only one party is the instructing party and a consumer, the other party bears at most the same share and only after the first party has evidenced payment (Section 656d BGB).
(4) Multiple sellers are jointly and severally liable. The commission arrangement becomes effective upon joinder of all owners entered in the land register or upon valid representation.

(5) The assessment basis is the notarized purchase price. If further valuable consideration is agreed in the course of the transaction — such as assumption of liabilities, buy-out or distance payments, or inventory sold with the property — the assessment basis increases accordingly insofar as those performances form part of the brokered transaction.
(6) A commission claim already earned does not lapse because the principal contract is later mutually cancelled or reversed; cases of initial invalidity remain unaffected.

sections.heading: § 6 Economically equivalent transactions and related persons
paragraphs: (1) If a closing results from Immonation’s activity, the commission claim remains intact even if the concluded contract differs in content from the evidenced opportunity or if a transaction with essentially the same economic result takes its place, provided that success is based on Immonation’s evidencing or brokerage.

(2) Conclusion with the customer is equivalent to conclusion by a person so closely connected to the customer personally, familially, legally, or economically that the contract economically benefits the customer. This includes in particular close relatives, companies controlled by or affiliated with the customer, and trustees or nominated purchasers engaged by the customer.

sections.heading: § 7 Due date and duty to notify
paragraphs: (1) Commission is earned and due upon conclusion of the principal contract; for contracts requiring notarization, upon notarization. It is payable after invoicing.

(2) Immonation is entitled to attend the conclusion of the principal contract. If the customer concludes the contract without Immonation’s involvement, the customer shall promptly inform Immonation of the closing and of the contractual contents relevant to commission calculation.

sections.heading: § 8 Rent and lease
paragraphs: (1) Immonation’s focus is on sales. Brokerage of rental or lease properties occurs only in individual cases and requires a separate agreement.

(2) For brokering commercial rental or lease contracts, the commission is three net cold rents or net leases plus statutory VAT, unless otherwise agreed for the property. The monthly net cold rent or net lease without operating and ancillary costs is decisive.

(3) For brokering residential tenancies, the “Bestellerprinzip” (Section 2 WoVermRG) applies: commission from the person seeking a tenancy is charged only if that person previously instructed Immonation in text form and Immonation acts exclusively on that instruction. Otherwise remuneration is agreed solely with the landlord.
(4) Remuneration agreed with the landlord is two net cold rents plus statutory VAT, unless otherwise agreed for the property.

sections.heading: § 9 Dual agency
paragraphs: In purchase contracts, Immonation may act commissionably for seller and buyer and is obliged to treat both sides fairly. When brokering residential tenancies, it may act commissionably for only one of the two sides. Mandatory statutory rules on the allocation of brokerage costs remain unaffected.

sections.heading: § 10 Prior knowledge
paragraphs: (1) If the customer already knows the evidenced property, the contractual opportunity, or the named contracting party, the customer shall notify Immonation without delay in text form and name the source of that knowledge in a comprehensible manner.

(2) Prior knowledge does not affect the commission claim if Immonation’s evidencing or brokerage was at least a contributing cause of the contract conclusion. Failure to notify or late notification may be taken into account when assessing causality.

sections.heading: § 11 Ending the cooperation; expenses
paragraphs: (1) The cooperation is not time-limited and may be ended by either side at any time with reasonable notice.

(2) If the property is marketed unsuccessfully for at least three months and the customer then ends the cooperation, no costs arise for the customer. The three-month period begins with Immonation’s first online listing of the property.

(3) If the customer ends the cooperation before expiry of those three months, Immonation may claim reimbursement of expenses actually incurred and evidenced up to that point (e.g. insertion, photo and video costs, travel costs), capped at a maximum of 25% of the commission expected upon success. The customer remains entitled to prove that no expenses or substantially lower expenses arose (Section 309 No. 5 BGB).
(4) If Immonation had no opportunity for online marketing before termination, paragraph 3 applies accordingly.

sections.heading: § 12 Private sale and withdrawal after reservation
paragraphs: (1) If the customer sells the property after instructing Immonation without first giving Immonation an opportunity to market via the intended channels, Immonation may invoice the services performed and evidenced up to that point in accordance with § 11.

(2) If a prospect evidenced by Immonation has made a binding reservation at the agreed purchase price and the customer then withdraws from the sale or concludes the principal contract with that prospect independently, Immonation is entitled to the agreed commission.

sections.heading: § 13 Continuing commission
paragraphs: If the customer concludes a principal contract within six months after ending the cooperation with a prospect whom Immonation had previously demonstrably named or evidenced, the agreed commission is payable provided the evidencing or brokerage was causal for the contract conclusion.

sections.heading: § 14 Confidentiality and disclosure of information
paragraphs: (1) Offers, exposés, and property documents provided by Immonation are confidential and intended solely for the customer; disclosure to third parties requires prior consent in text form.

(2) Disclosure remains permitted to the financing bank, notary, lawyer, or tax adviser, and to other advisers directly involved in reviewing or completing the specific transaction, provided they are bound to confidentiality and do not themselves act as purchaser or economic beneficiary.

(3) If unauthorized disclosure causes a third party to conclude the principal contract, Immonation may claim damages; the damage may in particular consist of lost commission. The customer remains entitled to prove that no damage or a lesser damage arose.

sections.heading: § 15 Liability
paragraphs: (1) Immonation forwards third-party information unchecked; checking it for accuracy and completeness is the customer’s responsibility.

(2) For slight negligence, Immonation is liable only for breach of material contractual duties and limited to the contract-typical, foreseeable damage. Liability for intent and gross negligence, for damage from injury to life, body, or health, and under the Product Liability Act remains unaffected.

sections.heading: § 16 Right of withdrawal for consumers
paragraphs: If a consumer concludes the contract by distance selling or away from business premises (e.g. at an appointment in the property), the consumer has a statutory right of withdrawal of 14 days (Sections 312b, 312g, 355 BGB). Details follow from the separately provided withdrawal information and model withdrawal form. If the consumer expressly requests performance to begin before the period expires, proportional compensation for value may arise upon withdrawal; complete performance before expiry may cause the right of withdrawal to lapse.

sections.heading: § 17 Limitation
paragraphs: Claims of the customer against Immonation become time-barred after three years unless the law provides a shorter period or a different period for specific claims.

sections.heading: § 18 Data protection
paragraphs: Immonation processes personal data under the GDPR and BDSG. Details are set out in the privacy policy on the website.

sections.heading: § 19 Final provisions
paragraphs: (1) Amendments and supplements require text form.
(2) If a provision is invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions is unaffected; statutory rules replace the invalid provision.

(3) German law applies. Place of performance and — where the customer is a merchant, a legal entity under public law, or a special fund under public law — place of jurisdiction is Fürth. Statutory places of jurisdiction apply vis-à-vis consumers.

metadata.title: Property sale process: 10 clear steps
metadata.description: How a property sale works with Immonation: ten clear steps from property intake and valuation to the notary appointment and key handover.

hero.title: The property sale process in 10 clear steps
hero.lede: A successful sale does not begin with a listing. It begins with complete information, a market-ready price, and a clear roadmap through to handover.

SalesProcess.answer: Our property sale process follows ten defined steps: we document the property and its records, assess market and price, agree the strategy, prepare the presentation, publish after your approval, and then manage enquiries, viewings, negotiation, the notary process, and handover.

steps.title: Instruction & property intake
steps.summary: We document your property completely and create a reliable basis for every decision that follows.
steps.detail: Once instructed, we take the time to build a complete picture. Property type, year of construction, condition, areas, plot data, features, modernisation work, and distinctive strengths are recorded together with the available documents.
activities: Record the property, areas, condition, and features systematically
Document distinctive strengths and modernisation work
Review available records and identify missing documents
steps.outcome: A complete evidence base prevents later surprises and makes the valuation and marketing defensible.

steps.title: Valuation & market analysis
steps.summary: We determine a market-ready asking price using experience, data, and current comparable listings.
steps.detail: The valuation rests on three pillars: our sales experience with comparable properties in the region, current market data and professional valuation tools, and comparison with similar properties currently offered on the market.
activities: Assess regional sales experience and property characteristics
Evaluate current market data and professional valuation tools
Compare competing listings and the property's realistic market position
steps.outcome: You receive a well-founded basis for an achievable sale price, not a wish price or a price chosen merely to win the instruction.

steps.title: Sales strategy
steps.summary: Together we define the asking price, target group, sales arguments, and marketing route.
steps.detail: The right price and message determine whether the first weeks of peak attention are used well. Before launch, we define which buyers fit the property, which strengths matter most, and which channels will reach them.
activities: Agree a market-ready asking price
Define suitable buyer groups and persuasive property strengths
Plan marketing channels and approval points
steps.outcome: A clear launch protects the most valuable attention phase and reduces the need for later price corrections.

steps.title: Professional preparation
steps.summary: Photography, floor plans, brochure, and digital presentation show the property from its strongest perspective.
steps.detail: We prepare a clear property description, high-quality photography, and polished floor plans. Depending on the property, a virtual tour or clearly labelled visualisations add context. Our specialist network can prepare missing lender-ready measured plans and floor-area calculations.
activities: Create the brochure, property description, and professional imagery
Review, improve, or measure floor plans when required
Use 360° tours, drone imagery, or visualisation where they add value
steps.outcome: Buyers understand the location, rooms, and potential online and arrive better prepared for the next stage.

steps.title: Publication
steps.summary: After your approval, we launch the property on the relevant portals and through the right channels.
steps.detail: The property enters the market only after the agreed approvals. We combine relevant property portals with our buyer network and, where appropriate, target-group social communication and additional visibility measures.
activities: Present the brochure and marketing materials for approval
Publish on the relevant property portals
Activate the buyer network and suitable additional channels
steps.outcome: Your property appears where suitable buyers search, with one consistent and approved presentation.

steps.title: Enquiry management
steps.summary: We handle every enquiry, assess seriousness and creditworthiness, and keep the process clear.
steps.detail: Quality comes before quantity. We answer incoming enquiries, pre-assess prospective buyers, review seriousness and financial readiness, and document feedback. Engagement with the virtual tour can also support the qualification process.
activities: Handle incoming enquiries completely and promptly
Pre-qualify seriousness, buyer fit, and creditworthiness
Document feedback and next actions systematically
steps.outcome: You face fewer unnecessary appointments and gain a clear view of the demand that genuinely matters.

steps.title: Viewings
steps.summary: We present your property to serious buyers and manage each appointment with clear preparation and follow-up.
steps.detail: Viewings are arranged with pre-qualified buyers and conducted professionally. We prepare for likely questions, explain the property's decisive strengths, and obtain structured feedback after each appointment.
activities: Coordinate suitable appointments with qualified buyers
Present the property and its sales arguments professionally
Gather feedback and re-qualify continuing interest
steps.outcome: Viewings become informed decision appointments rather than casual property tourism.

steps.title: Offer & negotiation
steps.summary: We check the buyer and financing, assess the overall package, and negotiate in your interest.
steps.detail: An offer is not judged only by the number on the page. We review price and conditions, buyer profile, creditworthiness, and financing, then negotiate with the goal of a strong and secure completion.
activities: Review the offer's price, conditions, and timing
Assess the buyer profile, creditworthiness, and financing
Lead negotiations and coordination in your interest
steps.outcome: You decide on a checked overall package instead of relying only on the highest non-binding figure.

steps.title: Notary & notarisation
steps.summary: We coordinate the purchase agreement, notary office, and all parties through to notarisation.
steps.detail: Once terms are agreed, we support preparation of the purchase agreement, coordinate open points with the notary office, and keep seller, buyer, and finance partner aligned through to the notarisation appointment.
activities: Bring together the information needed for the purchase agreement
Coordinate open points with the buyer and notary office
Support the organisation of the notarisation appointment
steps.outcome: Every party works from the same information toward an orderly contractual completion.

steps.title: Handover & completion
steps.summary: We support the key handover, document meter readings, and remain available for outstanding points.
steps.detail: The process does not end with the signature. We organise the handover, prepare or support the record, document meter readings, and coordinate the final outstanding points between the parties.
activities: Organise the handover appointment between seller and buyer
Document the record, keys, and meter readings
Coordinate final outstanding points through to completion
steps.outcome: The change of ownership ends in a clear and orderly way, with one contact through the final step.

FloorPlansPage.serviceType: Measured survey, floor plans, and living-area calculation

metadata.title: Lender-ready floor plans & living-area calculation
metadata.description: Measured floor plans and a verifiable living-area calculation under the German Living Space Ordinance — surveyed on site by our own in-house engineer. For sales in Nuremberg, Fürth, Erlangen, and Zirndorf.

hero.title: Lender-ready floor plans and a living area that holds up
hero.lede: Old record drawings and sketches rarely survive review by the buyer's bank. Our engineer surveys your property on site, redraws the floor plan with full dimensions, and calculates the living area verifiably — before the first buyer asks.

FloorPlansPage.answer: A lender-ready floor plan is a to-scale, fully dimensioned drawing from which every room area can be recalculated independently — paired with a living-area calculation under the German Living Space Ordinance (WoFlV). This is exactly what the buyer's bank reviews before approving a loan. At Immonation an in-house engineer handles it: an on-site survey, a dimensioned redraw, and a verifiable area calculation. Without it, financing stalls — or the price gets renegotiated.

comparison.title: What a bank accepts — and what it does not
comparison.text: Both drawings carry the same kind of information: rooms, walls, openings. Only one of them can be checked. The difference is not the care taken in drawing it, but whether every area can be recalculated from the plan itself.
comparison.disclaimer: Both images are illustrative examples shown to demonstrate the difference. Neither is a client document produced by Immonation.

accepted.title: To-scale floor plan with full dimensioning
accepted.text: Every wall, opening, and room is dimensioned. A case handler can recalculate the living area independently, without ever having seen the property.
accepted.alt: Technical ground-floor plan with continuous dimension chains, room labels, and construction annotations.
criteria: Continuous dimension chains, external and internal
Scale, storey, and orientation clearly stated
Wall thicknesses, openings, and stairs drawn to scale
Every area can be recalculated without a site visit

rejected.title: Freehand sketch without verifiable dimensions
rejected.text: The sketch conveys an idea of the layout, nothing more. Without dimensions and scale the living area remains an assertion — for a financing review it is worthless.
rejected.alt: Hand-drawn floor plan sketch with furniture and room names, but without dimensions or scale.
criteria: Wall thicknesses drawn freehand rather than to scale
Unusable for the credit file and the brochure

scope.title: From the on-site survey to a verifiable calculation
scope.text: We work from the building, not from paper in the planning file. What comes out of it goes on unchanged into the brochure, the portals, and the credit file.

items.title: On-site survey
items.text: Our engineer measures every room personally: lengths, heights, sloping ceilings, bays, and recesses. The basis is the building as built, not as approved.

items.title: Dimensioned redraw
items.text: The survey becomes a to-scale floor plan for each storey — fully dimensioned, with room labels and areas, delivered digitally and ready to print.

items.title: Living-area calculation under WoFlV
items.text: Areas are determined under the Living Space Ordinance: sloping ceilings counted proportionally, balconies and terraces at the permitted rate, cellar and ancillary space listed separately.

items.title: Reconciliation with your documents
items.text: We reconcile the result against the declaration of division, building plans, and purchase contract. If the actual area differs, you learn it before marketing — not during negotiation.

impact.title: Why a defensible area governs both price and pace

items.title: Financing goes through
items.text: The buyer's bank checks the plan and the area before approving. When both are verifiable, follow-up queries disappear and the time to the notary appointment shortens.

items.title: You are not liable for wrong square metres
items.text: A living area overstated in the brochure can entitle the buyer to a price reduction after completion. A documented calculation removes the basis for that dispute.

items.title: No discount for uncertainty
items.text: A buyer who doubts the area prices that doubt into the offer. Evidenced figures take the argument away — the negotiation is about the property, not about the plan.

items.title: Deviations in apartment sales
items.text: In attic and maisonette apartments in particular, the declaration of division often differs from the actual living area. A current survey settles it early and for all sides.

related.title: One building block in the wider sales process
related.text: The survey and the floor plan come first: they are the basis for valuation, brochure, and financing. Our sales roadmap shows how the remaining steps follow on.

faq.title: Common questions about floor plans and living-area calculation

items.question: What is a lender-ready floor plan?
items.answer: A to-scale, fully dimensioned drawing for each storey from which every room area can be recalculated. Together with a living-area calculation under the Living Space Ordinance it forms the basis on which the financing bank determines the mortgage lending value.

items.question: Why does the bank ask for a floor plan at all?
items.answer: A bank finances the value of the property, not the purchase price. It derives that value from area, layout, and condition. Without a verifiable plan it has no basis — approval is delayed or comes in lower than expected.

items.question: Is an old record drawing from the planning file enough?
items.answer: Rarely. Planning files show the approved state, not the built one; attic conversions, relocated walls, and extensions are missing. We review existing plans and tell you whether reworking them is sufficient or a new survey is needed.

items.question: What does the survey by your engineer cost?
items.answer: For owners who commission a valuation from us, the survey is part of the free on-site valuation. You incur no upfront cost, and it commits you to nothing regarding a sale.

items.question: How is living area calculated under sloping ceilings?
items.answer: Under the Living Space Ordinance, areas count fully from two metres of height, at half between one and two metres, and not at all below that. Balconies and terraces usually count at a quarter. We list these rates separately in the calculation.

items.question: What happens if the actual area differs?
items.answer: We discuss it before marketing begins. An area corrected downwards is unwelcome but manageable. An overstated area can lead to a price reduction after the sale. We market on evidenced figures only.

cta.title: Have your area verified before the market does
cta.text: The free on-site valuation includes the survey by our engineer. You learn what your property is worth — and whether your documents would survive a financing review.

items.question: Where can I find information for my property type?
items.answer: The selling section contains dedicated guides for houses, apartments, land, and apartment buildings.

items.question: Do the location pages include current property prices?
items.answer: No. Without approved market data we do not publish supposedly current square-metre prices. The pages explain durable local factors instead.

items.question: Can I download checklists directly?
items.answer: Yes. The downloads page offers free templates (handover protocols and tenancy forms). Enter a valid email to unlock the PDFs and download them directly — nothing is sent to your inbox.

items.question: Does a guide replace personal advice?
items.answer: No. Guides support preparation; pricing, strategy, and legally relevant individual questions require a property-specific review.

LegalWithdrawal.title: Withdrawal information
LegalWithdrawal.lede: For consumers · Immonation GmbH · Nürnberger Straße 18 · 90513 Zirndorf · As of July 2026. The German version is authoritative.

sections.heading: Right of withdrawal
paragraphs: You have the right to withdraw from this contract within fourteen days without giving any reason. The withdrawal period is fourteen days from the day of the conclusion of the contract.

To exercise your right of withdrawal, you must inform us — Immonation GmbH, Nürnberger Straße 18, 90513 Zirndorf, Phone: 0911 212 838 90, Email: info@immonations.de — of your decision to withdraw from this contract by means of a clear statement (e.g. a letter sent by post or an email). You may use the attached model withdrawal form, but it is not obligatory.
To meet the withdrawal deadline, it is sufficient for you to send your communication concerning your exercise of the right of withdrawal before the withdrawal period has expired.

sections.heading: Effects of withdrawal
paragraphs: If you withdraw from this contract, we shall reimburse to you all payments received from you, including the costs of delivery (with the exception of the supplementary costs resulting from your choice of a type of delivery other than the least expensive type of standard delivery offered by us), without undue delay and in any event not later than fourteen days from the day on which we are informed about your decision to withdraw from this contract. We will carry out such reimbursement using the same means of payment as you used for the initial transaction, unless you have expressly agreed otherwise; in any event, you will not incur any fees as a result of such reimbursement.

If you requested that the performance of services begin during the withdrawal period, you shall pay us an amount which is in proportion to what has been provided until you have communicated to us your withdrawal from this contract, in comparison with the full coverage of the contract.

sections.heading: Early expiry of the right of withdrawal
paragraphs: Your right of withdrawal expires in the case of a contract for the provision of services if we have fully performed the service and began performance only after you gave your express consent and at the same time confirmed your knowledge that you lose your right of withdrawal upon full performance of the contract by us.
